executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO covering October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian influenza A(H5N1) continues to generate concern with repeated updates indicating sustained zoonotic risk in the Americas region. Vector-borne diseases including dengue and chikungunya are circulating in the Americas, while respiratory threats including seasonal influenza, RSV, and pertussis are showing elevated activity across multiple hemispheres. Mpox transmission in the Americas and measles resurgence signal ongoing vaccine-preventable disease pressure.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous biological threats are active across the Americas and Europe, with avian influenza A(H5N1) zoonotic spillover, dengue, pertussis resurgence, and mpox representing the highest-priority concerns requiring coordinated public health response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple successive epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing zoonotic activity
Repeated PAHO alerts suggest sustained animal-to-human spillover risk across the Americas
Animal reservoir detections prompting human surveillance escalation
threats.action: Enhance zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces, enforce biosafety protocols at poultry and livestock facilities, pre-position antiviral stockpiles, and monitor for human cases with potential exposure

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating active circulation
Historical hyperendemicity across Latin America and the Caribbean elevates baseline risk
Concurrent chikungunya circulation suggests Aedes aegypti mosquito vector pressure is high
threats.action: Strengthen vector control programs, enhance case surveillance and serotyping, issue clinical guidance to healthcare providers, and prepare health system capacity for potential surge

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza
signals: PAHO alert issued April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Previous December 2025 alert documented simultaneous Northern Hemisphere season onset
January 2026 alert flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation creating dual respiratory burden
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake particularly in Southern Hemisphere ahead of peak season, strengthen syndromic surveillance, and ensure antiviral treatment availability in clinical settings

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating persistent transmission
Repeated alerts within three months suggest ongoing resurgence beyond seasonal baseline
Risk to unvaccinated infants and immunocompromised populations is significant
threats.action: Accelerate catch-up vaccination campaigns, reinforce maternal Tdap vaccination programs, increase laboratory confirmation capacity, and issue guidance to clinicians on early recognition and treatment

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas
Sustained regional circulation following global outbreak trajectory
Risk of clade-specific severity warrants ongoing genomic surveillance
threats.action: Maintain vaccination access for high-risk populations, conduct genomic sequencing to monitor clade distribution, enhance contact tracing infrastructure, and coordinate cross-border information sharing

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue virus indicates high Aedes vector activity across endemic zones
Potential for spread to naive populations in areas with competent vectors
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya surveillance with dengue monitoring programs, conduct vector control operations, and provide clinical guidance on differential diagnosis and case management

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating cases or elevated risk
Enzootic transmission cycles in sylvatic areas pose ongoing spillover risk to unvaccinated humans
Vaccination coverage gaps in at-risk populations remain a concern
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in endemic and at-risk zones, investigate reported cases for epizootic activity, and reinforce pre-travel vaccination requirements for affected regions

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 signaling resurgence risk or confirmed cases
Americas region had achieved measles elimination status making any reintroduction a high-priority signal
Vaccine coverage gaps likely driven by COVID-19 pandemic disruptions remain unaddressed
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments, implement outbreak response immunization in affected areas, strengthen case-based surveillance and genotyping, and address immunization catch-up for missed cohorts

diseases: Communicable Disease Threats (ECDC weekly monitoring covering multiple pathogens including influenza, COVID-19, and emerging threats)

amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific alerts were identified in the provided report titles; however, pertussis resurgence may warrant monitoring of macrolide treatment response
Repeat seasonal influenza alerts across hemispheres underscore the importance of monitoring antiviral resistance to oseltamivir and other neuraminidase inhibitors in circulating strains
emergingPatterns: Dual-hemisphere simultaneous influenza burden documented in late 2025 and early 2026 suggests increased year-round respiratory pathogen pressure

Multiple vector-borne disease alerts (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) issued in close succession indicate elevated Aedes aegypti vector activity across the Americas potentially linked to climate-driven range expansion
Three PAHO pertussis updates within four months indicate a resurgence pattern consistent with waning immunity and pandemic-era vaccination gaps
Concurrent mpox and measles alerts suggest broader vaccine-preventable disease surveillance gaps across the Americas region
Avian influenza A(H5N1) generating sustained alerts across two calendar years indicates persistent enzootic establishment in the Americas with ongoing zoonotic spillover potential
